tasks: Other:Conditional Generation for Hate Speech Detection
outputs: sequences of labels for offensiveness, group detection, group identification, and hate speech classification
The model generates predictions for subtasks (offensiveness, group detection, group identification) before generating the final hate speech label in a conditional generation setup.

changes_made.explanation: This paper is about hate speech detection, which is a classification task, not natural language generation. While they use a conditional generation framework, they are generating structured labels (Yes/No, Group/Individual/None, group identities) rather than free-form natural language. This is classification reformulated as sequence generation, not NLG evaluation.

The paper uses F1-score to evaluate classification performance, not to evaluate generated natural language text. Since this is not an NLG paper, these metrics are for classification evaluation, not NLG evaluation.
No LLMs are used as judges in this paper.
No human evaluation of generated outputs is conducted in this paper.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about hate speech detection, not natural language generation evaluation. While it uses a conditional generation framework (BART model generating sequences of labels), this is essentially a classification task reformulated as sequence generation. The outputs are structured labels (Yes/No, categorical choices, group identities) rather than free-form natural language text. Therefore, it does not qualify as an NLG evaluation paper and should not be included in the NLG evaluation metadata collection.
